field_photo_quickcheck.heading: How to identify Chloris andropogonoides in the field
steps: 1 · FIELD HEAD: begin with real source-identified panel 4, which connects one narrow windmill seedhead to its flowering stem, and with panels 0 and 3 for fully spread mature raceme hubs. The two new arrows on panel 3 mark only photographed hub and a long attached raceme.
2 · DEVELOPMENT: panel 1 is a real source-identified young/developing head whose slender rays remain mostly upright, not a distinct alternate grass species.

3 · LEAF/SHEATH: panel 4 displays lower narrow green leaves, overlapping pale sheaths and attached culm. Its new lower arrow does NOT point to roots. Rooted crown and lower rooting stems were not captured.

4 · INNER LIGULE: the short erose/ciliate membrane reported by the Hill Country treatment is NOT resolved in the gallery; photograph an opened true blade–sheath junction at 10–20× with a 1-mm ruler, rather than inventing a hair-fringe arrow.

5 · MATURE SPIKELET: published Chloris key calls for one rudimentary sterile floret and fewer than ten spikelets per cm of raceme. These photos are NOT ruler-scaled. Photograph complete ripe spikelets under lens and separate glumes, fertile lemma, sterile lemma and each awn insertion with mm scale.

6 · COMPARE: the last two panels are DIFFERENT species C. virgata and C. verticillata, and any hybrid/intermediate windmillgrass must remain uncertain without an examined voucher. Do not infer county nativity or microspecies ID from wheel silhouette.

field_id_measured_key_20261023.reference: Mexican Chloris taxonomic treatment and dichotomous key
field_id_measured_key_20261023.field_rule: In the treatment's perennial Chloris key, C. andropogonoides has one rudimentary floret, radiating racemes in one whorl and fewer than 10 spikelets per centimeter. The sterile lemma measures approximately 1–2 mm long and 0.3–0.5 mm wide. These are specimen measurements, not traits measured from current gallery photographs.
field_id_measured_key_20261023.compare: C. cucullata has racemes in multiple whorls and densely packed spikelets (>10/cm) in this key. C. virgata is keyed as an annual with a different sterile-lemma shape; do not separate on habit silhouette alone.
what_to_measure: Collect one attached mature raceme; record whether branches arise from one whorl or several
On a 1 cm segment of one mature raceme, count spikelets, using a millimeter scale
Under 10–20x magnification expose one mature spikelet and its single rudimentary floret
Photograph and measure the sterile lemma, expected 1–2 × 0.3–0.5 mm by this key
Photograph glumes, lowest fertile floret, awn insertion and the true ligule separately
field_id_measured_key_20261023.image_claims: No microscopic arrows added: the six GitHub JPEGs have not been inspected sufficiently to claim that sterile lemma measurements are visible.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — ONE WHORL OF LONG SLIM RAYS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Trace the entire flowering axis: many slender radiating racemes from one main whorl.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Start with CC0 panel 4: trace the thin flowering culm to its main starburst hub and count actual long narrow arms; compare the Cleveland Powell CC BY open-wheel panels 0 and 3, then contrast the developing compressed head in panel 1. The Mexican taxonomic key characterizes C. andropogonoides by generally one radiating whorl and fewer than ten spikelets per centimeter of an attached mature raceme. No image contains a usable true 1-cm measuring scale for that count. Some look-alike Chloris and hybrids overlap, so never certify from arm number or silhouette alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE ATTACHED HEAD AND ONE-WHORL HUB PHOTOGRAPHED; 1-CM RACEME COUNT MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOTED BASE, TRUE LIGULE AND COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Find the actual inner membranous ligule, reported up to about 1 mm, not loose collar hairs.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The same CC0 exact-source photo (panel 4) shows a thin attached culm, leaf blades and overlapping pale lower sheaths; roots and the true inner blade–sheath ligule are NOT in focus or exposed. Hagenbuch and Lemke's Hill Country key describes a short membranous ligule around 1 mm, truncate/erose and sometimes sparsely ciliate. The next specimen photo must show a truly connected fibrous-root crown and any lower rooting nodes, plus a separately peeled actual blade–sheath junction with a 1-mm scale. Do not label a white lower leaf sheath as a ligule or assert a stolon from the photo.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PARTIAL SAME-SHOOT BASAL SHEATH HABIT VISIBLE; ROOTS/TRUE LIGULE UNPHOTOGRAPHED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · SPIKELET, BOTH GLUMES AND FLORET COUNT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Examine a mature one-sided raceme under 10–20×; separate glumes from the fertile and reduced sterile florets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 3 and 2 are REAL attached unilateral narrow flowering branches and panel 0 shows their full hub. Published species treatments describe one rudimentary upper floret, and a useful practical check is fewer than ten mature spikelets per centimeter of the raceme. Neither hand nor finger gives an actual mm scale; zooming these JPEGs cannot establish a measured 1-cm count, glume boundaries or the number of tiny florets. Photograph a true 1-cm segment and separately opened spikelets under 10–20×.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE ATTACHED RACEMES — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO THREE DISSECTED SPIKELETS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FERTILE LEMMA, STERILE LEMMA AND AWNS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma about 2–4.6 mm; single rudimentary sterile lemma about 1–2 × 0.3–0.5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The real archived panels illustrate thin rays and the gross bract-covered spikelets only; they do NOT yet resolve fertile versus reduced sterile lemma, actual inserted awns or hairs at millimeter scale. The Mexican botanical treatment describes fertile lemmas around 2–4.6 mm and a reduced sterile lemma around 1–2 × 0.3–0.5 mm. Open one mature labelled same-voucher spikelet, retain both glumes and photograph each lemma and corresponding awn origin separately next to a real mm scale. Never use the different-species C. verticillata macro as proof for this taxon.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MICRO-ANATOMY — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO ATTACHMENTS AND SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOCAL WINDMILL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate one-whorl slender rays from tiered whorls, short crowded branches and feathery annual heads.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 4 is actual C. andropogonoides with a single narrow radiating hub and lower sheaths, while panel 5 is a DIFFERENT species (C. virgata, featherier compact head) and panel 6 a DIFFERENT species (C. verticillata, awned reproductive macro). Tumble windmillgrass may bear well-separated branch tiers; hooded windmillgrass C. cucullata has a different inflated sterile lemma. Source literature documents possible intermediates or hybrids; compare mature glumes and lemmas before determining an uncertain plant. No visual panel confirms a particular hybrid.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL OTHER-SPECIES COMPARISONS — ANATOMY STILL UNVERIFIED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE — TWO EXACT HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — rooted base and authentic ligule still missing
field_id_short_tiles.details: CURRENT RECONCILED COVERAGE: six exact-species JPEGs are physically archived (five CC BY or CC0 and one historical CC BY-NC). Five open-license exact-species photos appear in the gallery, with two differently labelled look-alike photo panels. Specific remaining needs: same-voucher exposed rooted base and actual rooting nodes if present; peeled inner membranous ligule with 1-mm ruler; full intact mature single whorl with scale for spikelet count per cm; measured mature opened glumes and fertile/reduced sterile lemmas with separately followed awns; independent rights/source checks and mobile/Pages QA. The old CC BY-NC photo is not automatically illegal on this declared noncommercial site, but its precise individual license version and final rights-filtered policy require independent verification before installation as a gallery panel. No new photographs archived in this pass.
